2607.11736.title: MET: Theory-Grounded and Culture-Aware Multilingual Moral Reasoning
2607.11736.paper_summary: Language models are increasingly used for moral decision-making across diverse linguistic and cultural contexts, yet existing work overlooks multilinguality on three aspects: 1) multilingual evaluation benchmarks use direct translation, failing to adapt culture-specific items; 2) inference-time methods for moral reasoning rely on static, English-centric scaffolds and lack grounding in moral theory; 3) training methods for moral decision-making typically require expensive supervision from stronger models or human annotators. We address these gaps with three contributions. First, we introduce MCLASH, a multilingual moral decision-making benchmark to capture culturally situated moral intuitions and social norms across languages. Second, we propose MET (Multilingual Ethics with Theory-grounded reasoning), a two-step prompting method built on expert-curated, theory-based grounds drawn from psychology and philosophy: the model first selects situation- and culture-specific grounds, then reasons over them in the native language of the user. Third, we introduce MET-D (MET-Distillation), which enhances the second step through a self-distillation training stage that requires no external supervision. MET-D improves macro-F1 over the base model on all three models of different sizes and families (Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, Gemma3-4B), by an average of 3.71 points on MCLASH and 4.23 on MMoralExceptQA, with a peak MCLASH gain of 12.94 points for Malay on Qwen3-8B. We further reveal that MET-D increases native-language reasoning by 62.13 points on average, and that beneficial grounds differ systematically across cultures. Together, these contributions open the path for culture-aligned, theory-grounded multilingual moral reasoning.
2607.11736.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型在多樣的語言和文化背景中越來越多地用於道德決策，但現有的研究在三個方面忽視了多語言性：1）多語言評估基準使用直接翻譯，未能適應文化特定項目；2）道德推理的推斷時間方法依賴靜態的以英語為中心的支架，缺乏道德理論的基礎；3）道德決策的訓練方法通常需要來自更強模型或人類標註者的昂貴監督。我們通過三個貢獻來解決這些空白。首先，我們介紹了 MCLASH，一個多語言道德決策基準，以捕捉跨語言的文化情境道德直覺和社會規範。其次，我們提出了 MET（多語言倫理與理論基礎推理），這是一種基於心理學和哲學的專家策劃、基於理論的兩步提示方法：模型首先選擇情境和文化特定的基礎，然後在用戶的母語中進行推理。第三，我們介紹了 MET-D（MET-蒸餾），通過一個不需要外部監督的自我蒸餾訓練階段來增強第二步。MET-D 在所有三個不同大小和類型的模型（Qwen3-4B、Qwen3-8B、Gemma3-4B）上，平均提高了 MCLASH 3.71 分，MMoralExceptQA 4.23 分，對於 Qwen3-8B 的馬來語，MCLASH 的峰值增益為 12.94 分。我們進一步揭示，MET-D 平均提高了 62.13 分的母語推理，並且有益的基礎在不同文化中系統性地不同。這些貢獻共同為文化對齊、理論基礎的多語言道德推理開辟了道路。
